submission.justification: Recommend Algorithm-L2 with a 37.0 GeV threshold. The project documents list Algorithm-L2 as an allowed candidate and state that all three candidates fit within the Level-1 FPGA resource budget. The rate allocation is 8 kHz, and the trigger emulation reports signal efficiency at the allocated rate. A scan over 20–60 GeV showed Algorithm-L2 outperforming the other candidates across the relevant region: representative best observed values were Algorithm-L2 near 35–37 GeV at about 93%, Algorithm-L3 near 31 GeV at about 86%, and Algorithm-L1 near 35–37 GeV at about 74%. Fine scans and repeated emulations around the Algorithm-L2 optimum gave the strongest performance at 37.0 GeV, with repeated runs averaging about 93.1% signal efficiency at the allocated rate, so this choice maximizes the observed signal efficiency while satisfying the hardware and threshold constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: Rate allocation document gives 8 kHz. The emulation tool reports signal efficiency at the allocated rate; scans over all three algorithms and thresholds in 20–60 GeV found Algorithm-L2 best. Repeated emulations at 37.0 GeV gave an average signal efficiency of about 93.1%, exceeding the best observed Algorithm-L3 result (~86.2%) and Algorithm-L1 result (~74.4%).
